input.prompt: Editorial cartoon in the tradition of 1960s American humour-magazine cartoons: pen-and-ink with crosshatching and loose watercolour wash, exaggerated caricature, warm and funny. A fussy little bookkeeper with sleeve garters, a green eyeshade and round spectacles stands on a tall stool at a towering old wooden ledger desk, ticking entries into an enormous open ledger with a long quill, sweating with concentration. Four old brass stock-ticker machines on pedestals around him each spew a long curling paper tape that snakes across the floor into the ledger; the tapes are completely blank. In the bottom foreground, a relaxed man in a cardigan sits in a comfy armchair with his feet up on a footstool, reading a magazine and smiling, a cup of coffee beside him. Two LARGE blank cream cardboard luggage tags hang on strings, each wide and horizontal, about a quarter of the picture's width: one hanging from the corner of the ledger desk, one hanging from the arm of the armchair. Every tag completely blank and evenly lit. Background: a warm golden-ochre watercolour wash filling the frame edge to edge, pigment blooms and paper grain. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no signs with writing, nothing written in the ledger or on the magazine.
